newsitem.title: MOROCCO: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - May 16.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Morocco economic weeklies - May 16.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Morocco's economic press. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Tourism Minister Mohamed Alaoui M'hamedi says "prohibitive fares" of state-owned airline Royal Air Maroc (RAM) deter foreign tourists.
- Domestic and foreign debt weighs heavily on the budget despite positive impact of privatisations and concession of water and electricity distribution to French Lyonnaise des Eaux.

- Mansour Kelada-Antoun, representative of World Bank International Finance Corporation, tells la Nouvelle Tribune "international interest for investing in Morocco is real but there is need to give more scope of action to foreign investors including infrastructure, airlines and telecommunications."

- Banque Marocaine pour le Commerce et l'Industrie is expected to approve a 300 million dirham ($31.9 million) capital increase during its general assembly on June 5, to extend network of branches and improve management.
- Ports traffic increased to 14.7 million tonnes during first quarter of 1997 from 13.8 million tonnes the same period last year owing to hydrocarbons and phosphates.
- The state signed accord with agriculture and agro-industry sectors to enhance quality of rural life, protect domestic output and extend irrigated land and research.
